To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Illinois State Board of Higher Education should plan for a substantial increase in the state's supply of degree recipients in most fields and that the state should plan for a large increase in the number of college graduates in most fields.

(1) the demand for educated manpower in Illinois is expected to grow at a rapid rate in the coming decade, (2) the supply of college graduates is likely to grow at a much slower rate, and (3) there will be a large surplus of educated workers in Illinois in the coming decade and the magnitude of the surplus will increase as the future becomes more distant.

the Illinois higher education system will be producing a large surplus of degree recipients under any reasonable assumptions about the future demand for college graduates and that the surplus will be largest for the humanities and smallest for the natural sciences.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the state of Illinois will be faced in 1975 with a large oversupply of college graduates in most fields and that this situation is likely to persist into 1980.

the Illinois system should be planning for a large increase in the number of students enrolled in the system and that this should include an increase in the number and quality of the state's institutions.

the Illinois educational system will have a substantial surplus of college graduates in 1975-80 and that the state should consider reducing its educational expenditures and/or increasing its educational output.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the demand for college graduates is likely to be quite high in 1980 but that the supply of graduates from Illinois is likely to be even higher, resulting in a large surplus of degree recipients.

the Illinois system of education is currently producing more graduates than are required by the state economy and that the system will continue to produce more graduates than will be required for at least the next decade.
the Illinois system of colleges and universities will have to plan to educate many more students than the state will be able to employ in the 1975-80 period.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supply of degree recipients is expected to increase at a faster rate than the national demand for college-educated manpower.

, in the face of a large and growing oversupply of college graduates, it will be necessary for Illinois to restructure its educational system so that it will be more responsive to the manpower demands of the economy.
, in the absence of a dramatic change in the economic structure of our state or nation, the Illinois system will continue to have an oversupply of degree recipients in most academic disciplines.
